summary: The settlement stall on INC-010 is most likely caused by the order-service v2.16.0 schema release at 07:40Z, which renamed the OrderExecuted field qty→quantity and bumped the schema header to v2, producing messages that settlement-service's v1 deserializer cannot parse (top hypothesis H1, confidence 0.60, medium). The signature is unambiguous on the consumer side: a repeated "missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)" error on the same offset orders-3@8841207 from 07:42:14Z, escalating into a poison-message retry loop that blocks partition 3, with lag climbing from ~38 to ~60k and throughput collapsing to ~0.4 req/s. Competing explanations were rejected: no rebalance/connection/DB-timeout errors exist in the log stream, resource metrics show no exhaustion and zero restarts, and the other consumer (notification-service) and producer (payment-service) on the shared broker are healthy, ruling out shared broker/DB faults. The reporter's suspicion of the 07:35Z poll-setting change is not supported — it produces no signal at 07:35 and cannot mechanistically block a partition. Confidence is capped at medium because producer-side emission of v2 records was not directly observed and broker/queue metrics were never queried.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change (qty→quantity) produced unconsumable OrderExecuted events
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service v2.16.0 (deployed 07:40Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty→quantity and bumped the schema version header to v2. settlement-service's avro/deserializer still expects v1 and requires 'qty', so the first v2 OrderExecuted message to land on orders-3@8841207 (07:42:14Z) fails to deserialize; because the offset is never committed, the partition is blocked, retries accumulate as a poison-message loop, and consumer lag grows without bound while throughput drops to ~zero. The fault originates in the producer's schema release, not in settlement-service.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.16.0 deployed at 07:40Z, renaming OrderExecuted qty->quantity and bumping event schema header to v2
The deployer begins emitting v2 OrderExecuted records onto the shared orders topic consumed by settlement-service
Settlement lag departs from its flat ~38-55 baseline at the 07:41 bucket and grows monotonically to ~60k
Settlement throughput collapses from ~61-63 req/s to ~0.41 by the 07:48 bucket
First logged error at 07:42:14Z is a deserialization failure on orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2), repeated 213x
From 07:44:51Z the same offset becomes a poison message; retries in the tens of thousands block partition 3
The only error stream is schema/poison-message; no fetch, rebalance, connection, DB-timeout or RPC signatures
Downstream latency and pod resources are flat/exhaustion-free, so nothing else is blocking the consumer

assumptions: order-service actually began publishing v2 OrderExecuted records at 07:40Z — not directly confirmed (F21: no order-service log lines containing 'quantity'; producer-side emission unverified)
orders-3 is the partition carrying the newly-emitted v2 records
The 07:41 lag-onset bucket and the 07:42:14Z first error are within the same onset event given ~11-minute bucket resolution

ranked_hypotheses.title: Consumer poll-settings change on settlement-service degraded consumption (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The settlement-service config change at 07:35Z reducing consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 caused rebalances / inefficient polling such that the consumer stopped making progress, driving lag growth and zero settlements posted. Under this reading the schema error is a symptom of the same degraded consumer (slow processing exposes/exacerbates the failing offset) rather than the cause.

causal_chain.claim: Smaller poll batches cause session-timeout-driven rebalances / repeated reprocessing, stalling the consumer group
Consumption stalls, zero settlements posted, lag climbs to ~60k

assumptions: max.poll.records=200 alone can trigger rebalance/partition-loss on this consumer group
The consumer group never logged a rebalance warning (none were retrievable, F21)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanistically contradicted: the error stream contains zero rebalance/session-timeout/fetch errors (F13) and the dominant signature is a schema deserialization failure (F11) which is unrelated to poll batch size. Timing also fails: order-service and its request_rate are flat across 07:35 while the collapse aligns with the 07:40Z signal (F16, F8), and lag/throughput onset (~07:41/07:40) is better explained by the deploy than the config change. Smaller poll batches would reduce throughput per poll, not produce a hard zero with a blocked partition.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared broker or shared ledger-db dependency failing (settlement as victim)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared kafka broker (queue-consume) or shared ledger-db (postgres, four writers) degraded — broker rebalance/ISR/leadership loss, or DB slowness from another writer — blocking settlement-service mid-processing so lag accumulates.

causal_chain.claim: Shared broker or shared DB degrades
Settlement-service consumers stall or block on I/O
Lag grows and zero settlements post

assumptions: A shared-component degradation occurred without any config change on the broker (F6 found none)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: notification-service, the other consumer of the same broker, shows no error at onset (F20); payment-service, the other producer, is flat (F19); downstream call latency is flat with no DB-timeout signature (F18); error stream has no connection/reset/fetch/DB-timeout lines (F13); no broker config change in window (F6). No positive evidence for a shared-component failure.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / broker-side fault driven by a change (CPU, GC, connections, partition reassignment)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Load or a change drove settlement-service into CPU/memory/thread/connection exhaustion, or a broker-side partition reassignment removed the consumer's assignment (as in the HIST-112 precedent), stalling consumption while lag grows.

causal_chain.claim: Consumer cannot process, lag grows unbounded

assumptions: A partition reassignment happened at ~07:40 despite no broker config change (F6)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: settlement-service pod metrics show no exhaustion: cpu flat ~68-71%, memory flat ~49-51%, db_pool_in_use flat ~6, zero restarts (F14). No rebalance/partition-assignment errors in the log stream (F13), and the other consumer on the broker is unaffected (F20). The only support is an UNVERIFIED prior-incident precedent (F7), which is weak evidence.

facts.statement: The only deployment across all services in the window was order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (author a.khan), which renamed the OrderExecuted event field qty -> quantity, added field 'venue', and added event schema version header v2; it is live and was not rolled back.
The only config change across all services in the window was on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records reduced from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z.

The dominant settlement-service error signature is a deserialization/schema failure, first at 2026-05-12T07:42:14Z and repeated 213 times through 09:58:31Z: "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)" — the same offset orders-3@8841207 recurs in every occurrence.

The error escalated into a poison-message retry loop on the same partition from 2026-05-12T07:44:51Z (196 occurrences, attempts in the tens of thousands, e.g. attempt 92490), reporting 'partition blocked' on orders-3.

All 409 matched settlement-service log records in 07:00-09:59 were ERROR level, and the only two patterns are the deserialization failure and the poison-message/partition-blocked retry; no fetch/publish errors, rebalance storms, connection resets, DB timeouts or RPC failures appear.

Consumer lag on settlement-service switched from a flat baseline of ~38-55 messages to sustained growth at the 07:41 bucket (avg 206 -> 1063 -> 3688), reaching avg 60412/max 61605 by 09:56 — a hard departure from baseline.
Throughput collapsed in the same bucket as the lag onset: request_rate fell from ~61-63 req/s (07:32 bucket) to avg 16.32 (07:40) and to a flat ~0.40-0.41 for the remainder of the window.
settlement-service pod/resource metrics show no exhaustion: cpu_pct rose to ~68-71 and held flat, memory_pct ~49-51 flat, db_pool_in_use ~5.8-6.2 flat, restarts 0.0 for the entire window.
Downstream call latency from settlement-service did not degrade at onset: latency_p99_ms flat across the stall (07:36 avg 243.6, 07:48 avg 238.79, 09:48 avg 237.22).
The other upstream producer to the shared broker, payment-service, is healthy at onset: request_rate flat (mean 99.96) and latency_p99_ms flat (mean 319.73).

The other consumer of the same shared broker, notification-service, shows no symptom at onset: error_rate flat through the window (mean 0.21), so a broker-side rebalance/common-component cause is not supported.
Upstream producer order-service shows no degradation at onset: error_rate flat and negligible for the whole window (mean 0.22), with no produce-error or publish-failure signature.
No config changes were found for the shared kafka broker in the window (count 0).

No settlement-service WARN/ERROR log lines with 'lag' and no order-service log lines containing 'quantity' were retrievable in the onset window (both queries returned 0 matches), so producer-side emission and consumer-rebalance warnings could not be directly confirmed.

settlement-service consumes from the shared kafka broker (queue-consume) and reads/writes the shared ledger-db; order-service (queue-produce) and payment-service (queue-produce) produce to that broker, and settlement-service and notification-service both consume from it.
ledger-db is shared by four writers (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service), so a change or load in any of them could affect settlement posting through the shared DB.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: order-service actually began publishing v2 OrderExecuted records at 07:40Z — producer-side emission was not directly confirmed (F21 returned no order-service log lines containing 'quantity').
ASSUMPTION: orders-3 is the partition carrying the newly-emitted v2 records and the failing offset orders-3@8841207 corresponds to a v2 message.
ASSUMPTION: the 07:41 lag-onset bucket and the 07:42:14Z first error fall within the same onset event, given ~11-minute bucket resolution.
ASSUMPTION: no other consumer of the orders topic failed in the same way outside the observed scope, i.e. the blast radius is limited to what was queried.
ASSUMPTION: the truncated log retrieval (40 of 409 matches) did not hide additional error signatures that would change the diagnosis.

timeline.event: settlement-service config change: consumer.max.poll.records reduced from 500 to 200 (only config change across all services; no signal accompanies it).
order-service v2.16.0 deployed (only deployment in window): OrderExecuted field qty renamed to quantity, venue added, schema version header bumped to v2.
settlement-service throughput collapses from ~61-63 req/s to a flat ~0.40-0.41 req/s.
Consumer lag departs baseline (~38-55 msgs) and begins sustained growth, reaching avg ~60k by 09:56.
First deserialization failure logged: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'.
Error escalates into a poison-message retry loop; partition 3 becomes blocked on the same offset orders-3@8841207.
Incident INC-010 reported: no settlements posted for ~40 min, consumer lag growing.
Lag plateaus at avg 60412/max 61605; the same schema error continues to repeat (213 occurrences total).

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back order-service from v2.16.0 to the prior release (revert a.khan's 07:40Z deploy) so it stops emitting v2 OrderExecuted records with the renamed qty→quantity field, then restart the settlement-service consumer group to release the blocked partition offset orders-3@8841207.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 is the leading root cause (confidence 0.60): the fault originates in the producer schema release, and the poison-message loop on orders-3 blocks partition consumption. Rollback plus consumer restart is the fail-fast mitigation that clears the stuck offset and restores throughput. Note: the poll-settings change (F1) is not believed causal, so do not rely on reverting it alone to restore service.

recommended_actions.action: Skip or dead-letter the poison offset orders-3@8841207 on the orders topic (or reset the settlement-service consumer group offset past it) to unblock partition 3 immediately if rollback cannot proceed within the SLO.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partition is blocked solely on a single unparseable offset (F12); bypassing that offset clears the block even before the producer is fixed, allowing other settlements to drain.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm the fix: verify order-service no longer publishes v2 qty-renamed OrderExecuted records, confirm settlement consumer lag trends back toward the ~38-55 baseline, request_rate recovers to ~61 req/s, and the deserialization error stops appearing in settlement-service logs.
recommended_actions.rationale: Closes the loop on the H1 mechanism by observing that throughput returns to the pre-incident baseline (F9, F10) and the schema error signature disappears (F11).

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT revert the 07:35Z settlement-service poll-settings change as a fix; keep it or revert independently only after the schema issue is resolved, then re-measure throughput.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 was rejected: the poll-settings change has no accompanying signal at 07:35 (F16) and cannot mechanistically block a partition; reverting it risks confusing the recovery signal.

recommended_actions.action: Add a producer/consumer schema contract gate (CI check or registry compatibility test) that fails order-service builds when an OrderExecuted field is renamed or a schema version header is bumped without a negotiated backward-compatible consumer upgrade.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of the exact failure mode in H1: an unconsumable v2 message blocking a partition (F2, F11).

recommended_actions.action: Add consumer-side alerting on partition-blocked / poison-message events and a consumer-lag SLO alert so a single blocked offset surfaces within minutes rather than as a 40-minute silent stall.
recommended_actions.rationale: The stall was detected only via reported symptoms; lag and the poison loop grew for ~40 minutes (F9, F12).

data_gaps: Broker/queue health metrics (topic partition status, broker CPU/IO, under-replicated partitions, ISR, request errors, consumer group rebalance count) were never queried due to tool-call budget exhaustion; broker/queue instability cannot be ruled in or out from the available data.

No log query at INFO level for the pre-onset window (07:35-07:50) completed (budget_exhausted), so what changed at 07:40-07:42 (config reload, consumer poll-setting change event) could not be confirmed from logs.
Producer-side confirmation that order-service v2.16.0 actually began emitting qty→quantity v2 OrderExecuted records is unverified: order-service logs returned 0 matches for 'quantity' (F21).
Neighbouring services (other consumers of the orders topic) were not queried, so the blast radius beyond settlement-service is undetermined.
Settlement-service log retrieval was truncated (40 of 409 matches returned), so rare additional error signatures could be hidden in the unreturned records.

Metric bucket resolution for order-service (660s) and payment-service/notification-service (840s) is coarser than the minute-level ordering needed, so the exact minute at which upstream behaviour changed cannot be pinned below the ~11-minute bucket.
Feature-flag changes across other services were not separately enumerated, so any flag-specific changes in the window may be missing.
Historical incident search returned only 5 results and did not surface precedents tied to poll-settings or producer schema-version changes; precedent set may be incomplete.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Observation that order-service v2.16.0 did NOT actually emit any v2 OrderExecuted records with the qty→quantity rename (e.g. producer-side logs or topic payload inspection showing v1 messages only) would remove the only mechanism linking the deploy to the failing offset.

Identification of a different, non-schema cause for the offset orders-3@8841207 deserialization failure — e.g. a corrupt or malformed message from another producer, or a schema-registry/deserializer change on the consumer side — would redirect the root cause away from H1.

Broker-side metrics showing a partition reassignment, ISR/leadership loss, or rebalance at ~07:40Z (as in the HIST-112 precedent, F7) that also affected notification-service would shift suspicion toward a shared broker fault (H3).

Evidence of consumer-group rebalance/session-timeout events on settlement-service coincident with the 07:35Z poll-settings change, or evidence that max.poll.records=200 alone caused partition loss, would resurrect H2.
Evidence that log truncation hid a dominant error signature other than the deserialization failure would weaken the consumer-side schema-failure diagnosis.

Confirmation that other consumers of the orders topic also failed on the same v2 messages would broaden (but not overturn) the H1 diagnosis; absence of such failures beyond settlement-service would narrow the blast radius.

findings.statement: The only config change across all services in the window was on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records reduced from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z (author m.das, reason 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes').

The only deployment across all services in the window was order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (author a.khan), which renamed the OrderExecuted event field qty -> quantity, added field 'venue', and added an event schema version header v2; status live, not rolled back.
settlement-service consumes from the shared kafka broker (queue-consume) and reads/writes the shared ledger-db (postgres, owner platform); both are shared components used by multiple services.

Upstream producers feeding the shared kafka broker are order-service (queue-produce) and payment-service (queue-produce); settlement-service and notification-service both consume from the same broker, so a broker-side rebalance would affect both consumers.

ledger-db is shared by four writers: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all have db edges to ledger-db, so a change or load in any of those can affect settlement posting through the shared DB.
No config changes were found for the shared kafka broker in the window (count 0).

Prior settlement-lag precedent: HIST-112 (2026-02-03) 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' — lag growing, settlements stuck, root cause 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance', resolved by restarting the consumer group; HIST-104 describes a Kafka broker rebalance storm causing consumer lag.

findings.statement: Timeline note: the settlement-service poll-settings change (07:35Z) precedes the order-service v2 schema deployment (07:40Z) by 5 minutes; both sit ~47 min before the 08:22Z report, so neither is immediately adjacent to the reported onset.

Consumer lag on settlement-service switches from a flat baseline of ~38-55 messages to sustained growth at the 07:41 bucket: 07:39 bucket avg 37.78/max 39.7 → 07:41 avg 206.44/max 386.63 → 07:43 avg 1063.21 → 07:49 avg 3688.8/max 3865.43, reaching avg 60412.45/max 61605.53 by 09:56. This is a hard departure from baseline, not a gradual pre-existing trend.

Throughput stopped essentially in the same bucket as the lag onset: request_rate was ~61-63 req/s through the 07:32 bucket, fell to avg 16.32 in the 07:40 bucket, and was down to avg 0.41/max 0.44 by the 07:48 bucket where it stayed flat (~0.40-0.41) for the rest of the window — i.e. zero settlements processed within ~2 minutes of the first deserialization error, not a long slow ramp.

Dominant error signature in settlement-service logs is a deserialization/schema failure, first at 2026-05-12T07:42:14Z and repeated 213 times through 09:58:31Z: "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)" — the same offset orders-3@8841207 recurs in every occurrence.

findings.statement: The error escalates into a poison-message retry loop on the same partition from 2026-05-12T07:44:51Z (196 occurrences, attempts in the tens of thousands, e.g. attempt 92490): "poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked" — i.e. the stuck offset blocks partition 3 consumption.

All 409 matched log records in 07:00-09:59 were ERROR level, and the only two patterns are the deserialization failure and the poison-message/partition-blocked retry. No fetch/publish errors, rebalance storms, connection resets, DB timeouts or RPC failures appear in the settlement-service error stream.

settlement-service pod/resource metrics show no exhaustion signal: cpu_pct went 27.48 (07:32 bucket) to ~58.26 (07:40) then held ~68-71 flat to the end (max 78.28); memory_pct stayed ~49-51 flat; db_pool_in_use ~5.8-6.2 flat (max 6.78); restarts 0.0 for the entire window.

The lag onset (~07:41 bucket) follows the reported consumer poll-setting change and precedes the first logged error (07:42:14Z) by about a minute; the first error is the schema mismatch on orders-3@8841207, and the poison/partition-blocked loop starts 07:44:51Z. The stall is upstream-inbound (an unprocessable inbound orders topic record), not a resource or broker-side fault visible on settlement-service.

Coarse 11-minute buckets make the lag onset and the order-service deploy look simultaneous, but at this resolution the poll-settings change at 07:35Z has no accompanying signal: order-service request_rate is flat across the change (07:36 bucket avg 230.97, 07:47 avg 231.53, vs 06:30 avg 225.64; window mean 231.5, min 197.21 max 256.25, missing_points 0), and settlement throughput collapse appears only in the 07:40-07:48 buckets — consistent with the 07:40Z deploy, not the 07:35Z config change.

Upstream producer order-service shows no degradation at onset: error_rate is flat and negligible for the whole window (07:25 avg 0.22, 07:36 avg 0.21, 07:47 avg 0.2, 07:58 avg 0.22; min 0.1 max 0.32, mean 0.22) — no produce-error or publish-failure signature appears, so there is no evidence of upstream topic-level producer failure.

Downstream call latency from settlement-service did NOT degrade at onset: latency_p99_ms is flat across the stall (07:36 avg 243.6, 07:48 avg 238.79, 08:00 avg 239.16, 09:48 avg 237.22; mean 238.27, missing_points 0) — no DB-timeout/RPC-failure latency signature, so downstream latency is not the first mover.

The other upstream producer to the shared broker, payment-service, is healthy at onset: request_rate flat (07:40 avg 99.78, 07:54 avg 99.36, mean 99.96, missing_points 0) and latency_p99_ms flat (07:40 avg 320.82, 07:54 avg 322.63, mean 319.73). payment-service therefore did not change its publish behaviour at 07:40Z.

The other consumer of the same shared broker, notification-service, shows no symptom at onset — a broker-side rebalance/common-component cause would be expected to affect it too, but its error_rate is flat through the window (07:26 avg 0.23, 07:40 avg 0.19, 07:54 avg 0.2, mean 0.21, missing_points 0), so broker-wide consumer disruption is not supported.

No settlement-service WARN/ERROR log lines with 'lag' and no order-service log lines containing 'quantity' were retrievable in the onset window (both queries returned 0 matches against data_range 04:00-09:59Z), so the producer-side view of the schema change and any consumer-rebalance warning could not be directly confirmed.
